summary: A first-person narrator, apparently a documentary maker with medical test records, visits a man in white in India who claims to be a miracle worker. In a sterile blue room with a bronze Dancing Shiva statue, he reviews her records without finding anything useful, deflects her question about children, and plays a hypnotic drone. He places his hands on her heart and tells her she is not breathing normally and that he feels no harmony, which she finds unsettling and recalls from a Zen meditation attempt in Kyoto.
one_line: A documentary-minded narrator visits a white-clad healer in India, who examines her records, plays a hypnotic drone, and diagnoses her breathing.
key_facts: The narrator visits a man dressed in white in India who claims to be a miracle worker.
The man's deep eyes snap open the moment the narrator enters, while he appears to be meditating in his chair.
He asks, "Did you bring your records?" without getting up.
Ramala discreetly disappears while the narrator produces her records from her briefcase.
The examination room is a sterile baby blue with no diplomas or photos.
A smaller bronze statue of the Dancing Shiva sits on a silver-inlaid table in the room.
The narrator thinks the man believes he is the Dancing Shiva, based on his flowing hair matching the bronze figure.
The narrator regrets not bringing a Betacam to video the encounter for a documentary.
The narrator states she has had every test known to science and none found anything wrong.
When asked whether he has children, the man replies, "All those who come here are my children."
The man says, "I haven't examined you yet," and states that he looks for different things than most physicians.
He activates a hypnotic drone that makes the narrator feel relaxed and full of hope.
He places his hands on the narrator's heart and listens to her chest, and his touch feels warm, then cold, then warm.
He tells her, "You're not breathing normally" and "I feel no harmony."
The narrator compares the feeling to her first attempt at Zen meditation in Kyoto.
